raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-AFW-HealthSecurityPhase3",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Armed conflict, ongoing regional violence, and mass population displacement across Central Africa may disrupt health service delivery and project operations.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare, consult upon, disclose, and implement Security Risk Assessments (SRAs) and Security Management Plans (SMPs) tailored to fragile and conflict contexts.",
      "evidence": "Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements... Boko Haram attacks in Cameroon and ongoing unrest in CAR"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Challenging macro-fiscal conditions, high national debt burdens, and low domestic health expenditure threaten the long-term financial sustainability of health security investments.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide technical assistance to prepare Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, enhance domestic resource mobilization, and introduce budget tracking for health security.",
      "evidence": "A challenging macro-fiscal outlook... low government funding... The country's high debt burden limits public investment in health"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Project implementation involving decentralized activities, workshops, and local capacity building presents financial management risks regarding questionable expenditures.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Customize project accounting software, update financial procedures manuals, strengthen internal audit oversight, and recruit independent external auditors across implementing agencies.",
      "evidence": "several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Fragmented or uncoordinated cross-border mechanisms among CEMAC, WAHO, and participating national governments could hinder rapid disease surveillance and outbreak response.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish formal collaboration protocols through the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC), sign cross-border information-sharing agreements, and harmonize regional operational guides.",
      "evidence": "Disease outbreaks often cross borders, making coordinated cross-border collaboration essential, as fragmented efforts hinder effective response."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Weak institutional and procurement capacities in fragile country contexts could cause procurement delays, governance issues, and weak contract management.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish dedicated Project Implementation Units with qualified procurement specialists, deploy hands-on World Bank supervision, and apply flexible procurement arrangements.",
      "evidence": "Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Increased deployment of frontline project workers and community health personnel poses substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop and implement SEA/SH Action Plans, recruit dedicated gender-based violence specialists, enforce codes of conduct, and establish accessible grievance mechanisms.",
      "evidence": "The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns of Sexual exploitation"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Inadequate stakeholder engagement may result in the exclusion of vulnerable, displaced, or marginalized populations from health security planning and emergency services.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adapt Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs) to country contexts, implement inclusive Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) strategies, and establish functional local GRMs.",
      "evidence": "Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Major public health emergencies and disease outbreaks may disrupt routine primary healthcare services, causing knock-on drops in essential care utilization.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop and update facility-level contingency plans, establish epidemic-ready primary healthcare networks, and routinely monitor essential service delivery indicators.",
      "evidence": "Prior epidemics show that future health emergencies could further strain health systems... interruptions in the health sector induce further knock-on effects"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Extreme climate events like severe flooding and droughts could damage healthcare infrastructure and accelerate outbreaks of vector- and water-borne diseases.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply green and resilient standards to facility refurbishments, integrate climate early warning systems into disease surveillance, and install solar power backup systems.",
      "evidence": "Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies in Central Africa and already has negative impacts on health systems"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "The generation, handling, and disposal of hazardous healthcare waste and laboratory reagents pose risks to occupational health and community safety.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Update and implement Healthcare Waste Management Plans, enforce biosafety and biosecurity protocols, and prepare site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans.",
      "evidence": "laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "High regional vulnerability to emerging zoonotic pathogens and increasing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) strains overburden existing diagnostic and surveillance systems.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Operationalize One Health national action plans, establish regional laboratory networks with genomic sequencing capacity, and implement antimicrobial stewardship programs.",
      "evidence": "Central African countries face high vulnerability to infectious disease outbreaks... Zoonotic outbreaks... have risen... Central Africa is also significantly burdened by antimicrobial resistance"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Gender disparities and systemic barriers severely restrict women's access to formal technical epidemiological and veterinary training and field roles.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement targeted female recruitment outreach, adopt flexible training formats, set explicit gender quotas for FETP and ISAVET courses, and monitor gender metrics.",
      "evidence": "women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making... women dominate low-paid frontline roles but are largely absent from technical positions"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Political instability and localized conflict in targeted areas (such as North-West and South-West Cameroon, CAR, or border zones) could physically restrict access to project sites.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt flexible implementation strategies in FCV areas, partner with local community actors, and enforce strict security management protocols.",
      "evidence": "Political instability, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions, may disrupt service delivery"
    }
  ]
}
